qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: High switching costs driven by regulatory spec-in instruments (Orbitrap mass spectrometry, chromatography, electron microscopy) embedded in validated FDA/EMA biopharma workflows, high-margin proprietary consumables and reagents, and the Fisher Scientific distribution network. Tangible operating ROIC consistently exceeds 40-55% with stable gross margins (~40-44%) and demonstrated ability to push 1.5-2.5% annual price increases above inflation. Key erosion risks include biopharma funding cycles, China domestic substitution, and NIH budget constraints.
qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Indispensable global leader in life sciences tools, analytical instruments, and biopharma services with >80% recurring revenue. Strong switching costs and regulatory lock-in sustain pricing above inflation. Highly cash generative (>95% multi-year FCF conversion) with peace-of-mind balance sheet ($9.85B cash, 5.46x interest coverage, A3/A- rating) capable of absorbing macro cycles. [5-10Y g: volume 4.0% + price 1.5% + mix/reinvestment 1.0% + margin expansion 0.5% + buybacks 1.0%]
qualitative.evidence: Revenue expanded from $18.3B in 2016 to $44.6B in FY2025 (guided $47.7-$48.2B for FY2026 with 4% organic growth). Operating income rose to $7.75B in 2025. Tangible operating ROIC of 43.7% in 2025 (55.1% in 2023, 47.6% in 2024); 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 9.15% reflecting $65.2B in goodwill and acquired intangibles from disciplined strategic acquisitions (Life Tech, Patheon, PPD, Olink). Multi-year FCF conversion stands at 97.2% with $6.0B Owner FCF in 2025 and $7.0B in 2024. Low capex intensity (~3.4% of revenue). Balance sheet maintains $9.85B in cash against $39.2B LT debt, with 5.46x EBIT interest coverage and $7.8B+ annual operating cash flow ensuring full self-funding capability across economic cycles.
